description: The Wood Horse in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1954 and 2014 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Horse is the Horse born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the seventh animal. It combines the Horse's energy with Wood's qualities. Wood Horse years between 1924 and 2044 are 1954 and 2014. The Horse's fixed element is Fire.

sections.heading: The Wood Horse personality
paragraphs: With Wood as its stem, the Horse gains a cooperative, idealistic layer on top of its love of freedom. The Horse's fixed element is Fire, and Wood generates Fire, so the stem is said to keep the Horse's flame supplied, much as kindling keeps a hearth bright. Wood Horses are commonly portrayed as friendly, imaginative and progressive, keen on new ideas and happiest when moving towards something worthwhile alongside others. Unlike some Horses, they often enjoy teamwork and can be thoughtful about how their choices affect people. The constant fuel makes them lively and hard to tire, though it also feeds the Horse's restlessness, so they may hop between enthusiasms before any one of them has had time to mature.

In the five-element scheme, Wood belongs to the east and to the green energy of early spring, and that seasonal image shapes how it colours an animal sign. A Wood stem tends to soften sharp edges and add warmth, curiosity and a cooperative instinct. Traditional texts associate it with benevolence, growth and the wish to build something that lasts beyond the self. People born under a Wood stem are often portrayed as principled, open-handed and hopeful about others. The caution usually attached to Wood is a habit of spreading energy thinly, saying yes to every request and feeling quietly hurt when generosity is not returned in kind.

sections.heading: Wood Horse at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

Sociable and principled, the Wood Horse brings momentum to teams that need someone to get things going. Tourism, outdoor education, journalism, campaigning and travelling sales are often suggested, since variety and cooperation are both rewarded there. It flourishes with a flexible schedule and colleagues who enjoy its enthusiasm, whereas rigid desk hours dampen it quickly. In love, the Wood Horse is cheerful, generous and keen on shared adventures, from road trips to learning a new dance together. It needs freedom and a partner who joins in rather than holds back. Friction comes when its appetite for variety looks like restlessness, and a partner wonders whether settled routines will ever appeal.

sections.heading: Wood Horse years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Wood Horse years are 1954 (February 3, 1954 to January 23, 1955) and 2014 (January 31, 2014 to February 18, 2015). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1954 anyone born before Feb 3 is a Water Snake, not a Wood Horse. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Wood Horse year is Yang, matching the Horse's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Jia-Wu, joining the heavenly stem Jia to the earthly branch Wu. Births just before each new year fall in the Water Snake year (before February 3, 1954) and the Water Snake year (before January 31, 2014), and births in the weeks after each Wood Horse year ends belong to the Wood Goat. The new year itself fell on a Wednesday in 1954 and Friday in 2014.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Horse
paragraphs: Wood Horses tend to do best when they pick a destination before setting off. Choosing a few long-term goals, and checking new opportunities against them, prevents energy from scattering. Because they are generous with time, they may agree to plans out of enthusiasm and regret it later; a twenty-four-hour rule before committing helps. Travel, outdoor sport and collaborative creative work suit their temperament well. Wood Horses also benefit from friends who are steadier than they are, offering a calm anchor. When their idealism finds a lasting outlet, Wood Horses become energetic champions of the causes they love.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Horse shares the Horse's San He trine with the Tiger and Dog (the Fire trine), its Liu He bond with the Goat, and its Liu Chong clash with the Rat. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Horse years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1954 (from February 3, 1954) and 2014 (from January 31, 2014). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Horse's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Horse's fixed element is Fire; in the five-element cycles wood generates Fire. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Horse?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Tiger and Dog (San He) and the Goat (Liu He). The Rat is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Horse called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Jia-Wu. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Jia, followed by its earthly branch, here Wu for the Horse, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Horse different from other Horses?
faq.answer: All Horses share energy, freedom and warm enthusiasm. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
